title: preprocessing.curate_data.reset_index
---



```python
preprocessing.curate_data.reset_index(df, index_name='DateTime', timezone='UTC')
```

Resets the index of the dataframe and assigns a name to the index column.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name       | Type                                           | Description                                                                    | Default      |
|------------|------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------|
| df         | [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | The input dataframe with a datetime index.                                     | _required_   |
| index_name | [str](`str`)                                   | The name to assign to the index column after resetting. Default is "DateTime". | `'DateTime'` |
| timezone   | [str](`str`)                                   | The timezone to localize the index to if it is naive. Default is "UTC".        | `'UTC'`      |

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                           | Description                                       |
|--------|------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
|        | [pd](`pandas`).[DataFrame](`pandas.DataFrame`) | pd.DataFrame: The dataframe with the reset index. |

## Examples {.doc-section .doc-section-examples}


::: {#293861da .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import pandas as pd
from spotforecast2_safe.preprocessing.curate_data import reset_index
date_rng = pd.date_range(start='2023-01-01', end='2023-01-02', freq='h')
data = pd.DataFrame(date_rng, columns=['date'])
data.set_index('date', inplace=True)
data['value'] = range(len(data))
reset_data = reset_index(data, index_name='DateTime')
print(reset_data.head())
```
